instruction: Filter and view men's Adidas shorts under $40.

metadata.explanation: Variation of NBA store filtering task. User must apply 4 filters: men's category, Adidas brand, shorts type, and under $40 price. Evaluator checks that all filters are present in HTML class elements and URL parameters, with no extra filters applied (is_other_exist: false).
metadata.verification: Reuses existing check_direct_json_object metric and get_active_tab_html_parse getter. Pattern matches original task structure.

llm_judge_reasons: Evaluator correctly uses category 'class&url' to check both HTML elements and URL for filter presence
All 4 instruction requirements (men, Adidas, shorts, under $40) are verified in the expected rules
The is_other_exist check appropriately ensures no unexpected filters are applied
Getter extracts filter text from class 'filter-selector-link' which is a standard pattern for e-commerce filters
URL verification provides additional validation that filters are actually applied to the search
Minor concern: Text matching is case-insensitive but may not handle variations in spacing or formatting
Minor concern: The getter relies on specific class name 'filter-selector-link' which may vary across different websites
Overall logic flow is sound: extract filters from HTML and URL, then compare against expected set
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Consider adding flexibility for text variations (e.g., 'Under $40' vs 'under $40', '$40 & Under' vs 'under $40')
Could benefit from fuzzy matching for filter text to handle minor formatting differences
Consider documenting that this evaluator is designed for NBA store or similar e-commerce sites with similar filter structures
